Here's the diagnosis:

**The problem is a WSL2 path mismatch.** Specstory (v1.11.0) is running inside WSL and looks for Cursor IDE sessions at the Linux-standard path (`~/.config/Cursor/`), which doesn't exist. Cursor's actual session data lives on the Windows side at `/mnt/c/Users/<your-user>/AppData/Roaming/Cursor/`.

There are two things you can try:

1. **Update Specstory to v1.12.0** — you're currently on `1.11.0-windows-support`, and the newer version may have better WSL2 detection. Check the [Specstory docs](https://docs.specstory.com/quickstart) for update instructions.

2. **Create a symlink** as a workaround to point Specstory to the Windows-side Cursor data:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.config
ln -s /mnt/c/Users/<YOUR_WINDOWS_USERNAME>/AppData/Roaming/Cursor ~/.config/Cursor
```

   Replace `<YOUR_WINDOWS_USERNAME>` with your actual Windows username.

The `sync` command in Terminal 4 didn't error — it just found no sessions, which is consistent with it not finding the Cursor IDE sessions directory either (it only checked VS Code Copilot IDE and found nothing).
